name: Near-Horizon Extreme Kerr Geometry
description: The vacuum geometry left when one looks only at the region just outside the horizon of a Kerr black hole spinning as fast as it can, known as NHEK. At every polar angle it is a circle fibred over anti-de Sitter space of two dimensions, it has no singularity and no asymptotically flat region, and the Kerr/CFT correspondence is built on it.
convention: We keep factors of $c$ and $G$ explicit, and the one scale is the length $r_0$, with $r_0^2 = 2GJ/c^3$ for a black hole of angular momentum $J$. The Ricci tensor is the standard contraction, $R_{\mu\nu} = R^\alpha{}_{\mu\alpha\nu}$.
history: How much of a black hole is left when you look only at the region just outside its horizon? For a Kerr black hole spinning as fast as it can, $J = GM^2/c$, the answer is a spacetime of its own, because the distance to the horizon along a surface of constant time is infinite: the hole sits at the bottom of a throat with no end [bardeen1999]. The charged version of that throat was an old friend by 1999, since the geometry near the horizon of an extreme Reissner-Nordström black hole is the Bertotti-Robinson universe, AdS$_2 \times S^2$ [bardeen1999]. That May James Bardeen and Gary Horowitz wanted the same thing for a hole that spins [bardeen1999]. Bardeen had seen the throat before: with Robert Wagoner in 1971 he had pushed a uniformly rotating disk to its extreme relativistic limit and found the outside of the disk turning into the throat of an extreme Kerr black hole [bardeen1971, bardeen1999].¶Their recipe is a zoom: step into coordinates that turn with the horizon, stretch the distance from the horizon by a factor $1/\lambda$, slow the clock by the same factor, and let $\lambda$ go to zero [bardeen1999]. The asymptotically flat region is pushed off to infinity, and a vacuum solution stays behind with a single parameter, the angular momentum $J$, which sets the overall scale and nothing else [bardeen1999, guica2009]. Kerr's black hole has two symmetries, a shift in time and a turn about the axis, and the throat doubles them to four, the group $SL(2,\mathbb{R}) \times U(1)$ [bardeen1999]. Along the axis the geometry is "precisely" a two dimensional anti-de Sitter space, in Bardeen and Horowitz's word, and at every other polar angle it is that space with a circle of $\phi$ twisted over it [bardeen1999, guica2009].¶Does the throat have an edge, or a singularity hiding in it? The coordinates that come out of the limit cover only a wedge, the way Poincaré coordinates cover a wedge of anti-de Sitter space, so Bardeen and Horowitz built global ones, $\tau$ and $y$, and followed every geodesic to infinite affine parameter [bardeen1999]. The throat is complete and "completely nonsingular", with two timelike boundaries at $y \to \pm\infty$ [bardeen1999]. No symmetry of the throat is a time translation everywhere: $\partial_\tau$ is timelike at every angle only for $y^2 < 1/3$, and beyond that it is spacelike near the equator, which Bardeen and Horowitz compared to Kerr's ergosphere [bardeen1999, amsel2009]. Waves that carry enough angular momentum travel all the way to the boundary, and one sent in from there scatters and returns with more energy than it started with [bardeen1999]. The sphere of $\theta$ and $\phi$ at each point of the throat is the horizon of the extreme hole, flattened by its spin, with the two polar caps of negative curvature that Larry Smarr found in 1973 on a Kerr horizon spinning this fast [smarr1973].¶Anti-de Sitter space had by 1999 become the place where gravity is traded for a field theory on the boundary, and the throat's boundary is timelike too, so Bardeen and Horowitz wrote that their solution "suggests the possibility of a dual quantum mechanical description" [bardeen1999, maldacena1998]. Nine years later Monica Guica, Thomas Hartman, Wei Song, and Andrew Strominger took the suggestion up, gave the throat the name NHEK, and wrote its Poincaré patch in an inverse radius, where the plane of time and radius is conformal to flat [guica2009]. Their model was J. David Brown and Marc Henneaux's 1986 treatment of anti-de Sitter space in three dimensions: choose how fast a perturbation must fall off at the boundary, then ask which changes of coordinates respect the choice [guica2009, brown1986]. For the throat those changes form a Virasoro algebra with central charge $c_L = 12J/\hbar$ [guica2009]. Cardy's formula, fed that central charge and the temperature $T_L = 1/2\pi$ of the extreme hole's vacuum, returns $S = 2\pi J/\hbar$, the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy of extreme Kerr [guica2009]. They conjectured that the extreme Kerr black hole is dual to a chiral conformal field theory in two dimensions, and they pointed at GRS 1915+105, whose measured spin is above $0.98$ of the maximum, as a hole whose dual would have $c_L \sim 2 \times 10^{79}$ [guica2009, mcclintock2006].¶Does anything live in the throat? Aaron Amsel, Horowitz, Donald Marolf, and Matthew Roberts went looking in June 2009 for solutions of the vacuum equations that approach the throat at its boundary, and argued that every one of them is the throat itself in other coordinates [amsel2009]. That same June, Óscar Dias, Harvey Reall, and Jorge Santos solved Saul Teukolsky's equation in the throat for a massless field of any spin and found no unstable mode with outgoing boundary conditions [dias2009kerr]. A black hole just short of extreme, taken to the same limit at a fixed temperature, gives the throat again, in coordinates that end at a horizon of their own [amsel2009]. Irene Bredberg, Hartman, Song, and Strominger called that patch near-NHEK and matched the scattering of waves off a nearly extreme Kerr black hole to a conformal field theory in a thermal state [bredberg2010]. Geoffrey Compère, reviewing the subject in 2017, cautioned that the entropy match is no microscopic counting, since nobody has written the dual theory down in terms of elementary fields [compere2017].¶Could a telescope ever look down the throat? For a hot spot circling just outside the horizon of a hole spinning near the limit, Samuel Gralla, Alexandru Lupsasca, and Strominger computed by hand what the Event Horizon Telescope would see [gralla2018]. Its light arrives on a vertical line segment at the edge of the hole's shadow, which they named the NHEKline, since the emission comes from the NHEK region [gralla2018]. The line disappears for an observer within about $47°$ of the spin axis, the polar angle at which a slice of the throat at fixed $\theta$ is locally an ordinary anti-de Sitter space of three dimensions [gralla2018, guica2009]. If such a line is ever seen, they wrote, it would be a "smoking gun" for a black hole of high spin [gralla2018].

related.text: The rotating black hole whose throat this is. Spin Kerr up to $a = GM/c^2$, zoom in on the horizon, and the throat remains [bardeen1999].
The throat of the extreme charged black hole, anti-de Sitter space of two dimensions times a round sphere. Bardeen and Horowitz called theirs "a vacuum analog" of it [bardeen1999].
Give the extreme hole charge as well as spin and its throat slides from this one to the Bertotti-Robinson throat as the charge grows [bardeen1999].
Along its axis the throat is exactly an anti-de Sitter space of two dimensions, and its boundary is timelike, as anti-de Sitter's is [bardeen1999].

coordinates.name: Poincaré

parameters.description: Scale of the throat, a length, with $r_0^2 = 2GJ/c^3 = 2G^2M^2/c^4$ for the extreme Kerr black hole of angular momentum $J$ and mass $M$ whose throat this is; the area of its horizon is $4\pi r_0^2$

coordinates.convention: We use Bardeen and Horowitz's coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$, which turn with the horizon, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time and $r$ a length. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.

coordinates.name: Poincaré, Inverse Radius

parameters.description: Scale of the throat, a length, with $r_0^2 = 2GJ/c^3 = 2G^2M^2/c^4$ for the extreme Kerr black hole of angular momentum $J$ and mass $M$ whose throat this is; the area of its horizon is $4\pi r_0^2$

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, x, \theta, \phi)$, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time and $x$ a length, related to the Poincaré chart by $rx = r_0^2$. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.

coordinates.name: Global

parameters.description: Scale of the throat, a length, with $r_0^2 = 2GJ/c^3 = 2G^2M^2/c^4$ for the extreme Kerr black hole of angular momentum $J$ and mass $M$ whose throat this is; the area of its horizon is $4\pi r_0^2$

coordinates.convention: We use Bardeen and Horowitz's global coordinates $(\tau, y, \theta, \phi)$, with $\tau$ and $y$ pure numbers, so $\tau$ is itself the chart's $x^0$. A dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter.

parameters.description: Scale of the throat, a length, with $r_0^2 = 2GJ/c^3 = 2G^2M^2/c^4$ for the extreme Kerr black hole of angular momentum $J$ and mass $M$ whose throat this is; the area of its horizon is $4\pi r_0^2$
Half the coordinate radius of the horizon of the patch, a length; the surface gravity of that horizon with respect to $t$ is $c^2k/r_0^2$, and at $k = 0$ the chart is the Poincaré chart

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$ adapted to a horizon of finite temperature at $r = 2k$, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time and $r$ and $k$ lengths. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.
